methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center (150 patients, 63.3% csPCa); radiologist vs precommercial AI version PAROS compared using biopsy as reference. McNemar's test for sensitivity/specificity comparison, Pearson correlation for measurements. Main limitation: single experienced reader (25 years experience), single 3T MRI scanner, retrospective design, clinically enriched cohort. Biparametric AI vs multiparametric radiologist (different input data).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort comparing diagnostic tools for csPCa detection on MRI; directly relevant to urologic imaging practice. However, single-center, single reader limits generalizability to less-experienced interpreters (which is stated goal). Findings suggest AI as decision-support tool rather than replacement.

reporting_quality.justification: Follows observational cohort reporting with clear methods (patient selection, MRI protocol, AI software description), results with sensitivity/specificity, PLR/NLR, and Limitations section. However, no data availability statement; use of non-commercial/pre-launch software version raises reproducibility questions; authors acknowledge need for larger prospective multi-center studies.

novelty_literature.justification: Compares commercial (PAROS) and experienced radiologist for csPCa detection; adds to growing AI diagnostic accuracy literature. Findings (comparable sensitivity/specificity, excellent rule-out) expected based on prior AI studies. Main contribution incremental rather than novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured with clear Introduction establishing clinical rationale, detailed Methods describing MRI protocol and AI tool, Results clearly presenting accuracy metrics, Discussion interpreting findings and acknowledging limitations appropriately. Some Discussion length regarding biparametric vs multiparametric comparison.

key_strengths: Addresses clinically relevant question: can AI-based PAROS achieve diagnostic performance comparable to experienced radiologist for csPCa detection?
Excellent rule-out capability documented (very low NLR ~0.1), supporting AI role in reducing unnecessary biopsies
Real-world comparison using histopathology reference standard; transparent reporting of both agreement and discordance between readers
Clear articulation of AI as decision-support tool rather than replacement, with appropriate clinical guidance
key_concerns: Single-center, single experienced reader design severely limits ability to evaluate AI's stated role as support for less-experienced readers
Clinically enriched cohort (63.3% csPCa prevalence, only 16 patients with PI-RADS 1-2) restricts generalizability to screening or low-risk populations
Biparametric AI vs multiparametric radiologist comparison introduces bias; authors acknowledge DCE role in PI-RADS v2.1 but cannot exclude influence on radiologist confidence
Use of pre-commercial trial software version raises reproducibility concerns; commercial version may differ materially
Modest sample size with verification bias (only patients undergoing biopsy included); prospective studies in balanced cohorts needed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective comparison of AI and radiologist for csPCa detection with appropriate statistical methods and transparent discussion of limitations. Single-center design with single reader and clinically enriched cohort limits generalizability. Tier 3 venue appropriate; recommend minor revisions addressing feasibility in multi-reader, lower-prevalence settings before publication.
